content: Etravirine significantly interacts with numerous medications by altering their metabolism, primarily through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. These interactions can either increase or decrease the levels and effects of the co-administered drugs, necessitating careful consideration of alternative therapies or dosage adjustments. Below are specific examples of these interactions: 1. Etravirine and Idelalisib: Etravirine reduces idelalisib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 2. Etravirine and Indinavir: Etravirine decreases indinavir levels unless indinavir is boosted with low-dose ritonavir. Avoid co-administration unless ritonavir is used. 3. Etravirine and Irinotecan: Etravirine reduces irinotecan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Etravirine and Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 5. Etravirine and Ivabradine: Etravirine decreases ivabradine levels. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. 6. Etravirine and Ivacaftor: Etravirine reduces ivacaftor levels significantly (~9-fold). Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 7. Etravirine and Venetoclax: Etravirine increases venetoclax levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50%. 8. Etravirine and Rifampin: Rifampin decreases etravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Etravirine and Simvastatin: Etravirine reduces simvastatin levels. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative lipid-lowering agents. 10. Etravirine and Siponimod: Etravirine decreases siponimod levels. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers, especially in patients with specific CYP2C9 genotypes (1/3 or 2/3). 11. Etravirine and Trazodone: Etravirine reduces trazodone levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative antidepressant. 12. Etravirine and Atorvastatin: Etravirine decreases atorvastatin levels. Monitor therapy closely and adjust the dose as needed. 13. Etravirine and Amiodarone: Amiodarone increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP2C9 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Etravirine and Alprazolam: Etravirine reduces alprazolam levels. Monitor therapy and adjust the dose if necessary. 15. Etravirine and Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases etravirine levels by inducing CYP2C9 metabolism. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and consider alternative therapies. 16. Etravirine and Aprepitant: Etravirine reduces aprepitant levels, while aprepitant increases etravirine levels. Use caution and monitor therapy. 17. Etravirine and Aripiprazole: Etravirine decreases aripiprazole levels. Monitor therapy and adjust the dose as needed. 18. Etravirine and Voriconazole: Voriconazole increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative antifungal. 19. Etravirine and ZanuBrutinib: Etravirine reduces zanubrutinib levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, increase the zanubrutinib dose to 320 mg twice daily. 20. Etravirine and Abiraterone: Etravirine decreases abiraterone levels. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is necessary, increase the abiraterone dosage frequency from once daily to twice daily. 21. Etravirine and Belumosudil: Etravirine reduces belumosudil levels. Increase the belumosudil dose to 200 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 22. Etravirine and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Etravirine reduces hydrocodone levels, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Use caution when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers. 23. Etravirine and Betrixaban: Etravirine increases betrixaban levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, followed by 40 mg daily. 24. Etravirine and Bortezomib: Etravirine reduces bortezomib levels. Monitor therapy and adjust the dose as needed. 25. Etravirine and Bosentan: Bosentan decreases etravirine levels by inducing CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. This list highlights the importance of understanding drug interactions involving etravirine, particularly its effects on CYP3A4 and other metabolic pathways.
